purpose: Separate actual Branch shipbuilding/survival dividend from fantasy acceleration, then screen younger hulls for Indian Ocean observation/submarine liaison/light-force reinforcement.

shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Yugumo_class: 3-5% shorter completion/fit-out clock; normally 2-4 weeks, not months
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Matsu_class: no major emergency acceleration before 1944; not a Jan-1944 reinforcement source
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.kaibokan_1943: 20-30 extra/accelerated orders; 1943 completion center 36-42, upper about 45; key effect is freeing fleet DD from slow convoy escort
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Chitose_Chiyoda: remain seaplane tenders, not converted to carriers
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Ise_Hyuga: remain conventional 12-gun battleships; no hybrid conversion downtime
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Nisshin: survives because historical New Georgia loss chain absent
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Ibuki: heavy-cruiser path; completion not before late Jun/early Jul 1944; irrelevant to Jan move
shipbuilding_branch_deltas.Taiho: Feb 1944 completion, then work-up; not Jan asset

survival_dividend.Yugumo_class: 16 hulls historically completed by 1944-01-01; seven of those historical pre-1944 losses are tied to absent Guadalcanal/Solomons operations and therefore return to the Branch pool unless branch-specific loss assigned
survival_dividend.Akizuki_class: six hulls completed by 1944-01-01; Teruzuki and Niizuki historical pre-1944 losses are absent in this Branch unless separately assigned
survival_dividend.warning: Kagero-class extra survival is probably substantial but must wait for 1941-early-1943 hull audit before being counted.

candidate_screen.name: Oyodo
candidate_screen.recommended_role: Singapore/Sabang mobile ISR, communications and submarine-report fusion headquarters; not a line-of-battle cruiser
candidate_screen.why: completed Feb 1943; fast; originally conceived around long-range reconnaissance/submarine-squadron command functions; Branch sensor/DF/contact-handoff improvements increase the value of this role
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: medium; currently Pacific/Combined-Fleet useful but less directly tied to a specific carrier air group than Agano

candidate_screen.name: Teruzuki
candidate_screen.recommended_role: AA/picket escort for mobile observation/light-force group
candidate_screen.why: Akizuki-class, mature by Jan 1944; historical Guadalcanal loss absent
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: medium-high because Akizuki hulls are scarce carrier escorts

candidate_screen.name: Niizuki
candidate_screen.recommended_role: radar/picket-oriented AA destroyer and night-contact relay
candidate_screen.why: Akizuki-class, completed Mar 1943; historical Kula Gulf loss absent
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: medium-high; use one of Teruzuki/Niizuki initially, not both unless RN enters Bay

candidate_screen.name: Kiyonami
candidate_screen.why: Yugumo-class mature early 1943; historical Solomon loss absent

candidate_screen.name: Suzunami
candidate_screen.why: Yugumo-class completed Jul 1943; historical Rabaul loss absent

candidate_screen.name: Hayanami
candidate_screen.why: Yugumo-class completed Jul 1943; enough work-up by Jan 1944

candidate_screen.name: Makinami_or_Onami
candidate_screen.recommended_role: additional torpedo DD if Pacific screen can release one
candidate_screen.why: mature Yugumo-class hulls whose historical late-1943 Solomon losses are absent

candidate_screen.name: Agano
candidate_screen.recommended_role: DesRon leader for a true offensive light-force interception group
candidate_screen.why: modern 35-knot-class light cruiser, mature; historical Rabaul/Scamp damage chain absent
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: high because it is naturally tied to Third Fleet/carrier destroyer organization; do not move merely because RN reaches Ceylon

candidate_screen.name: Noshiro
candidate_screen.why: completed Jun 1943 and mature by Jan
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: high because it is Second Fleet DesRon flagship; better as second escalation choice

candidate_screen.name: Yahagi
candidate_screen.why: completed 1943-12-29; still work-up/training in Jan; earliest serious transfer Feb

candidate_screen.name: Shimakaze
candidate_screen.recommended_role: high-speed intercept/reposition experiment only after fresh RN eastbound contact
candidate_screen.why: unique high-value experimental hull; not worth stripping from Central Pacific for routine presence

candidate_screen.name: Chitose_or_Chiyoda
candidate_screen.recommended_role: rear mobile seaplane maintenance/recon support at Singapore/Sabang/Mergui
candidate_screen.why: Branch did not convert them to carriers; this creates an observation-network asset that history did not have in this form at this date
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: medium; exact location/readiness must be traced before assignment

candidate_screen.name: Nisshin
candidate_screen.recommended_role: fast heavy-equipment/engineer/AA transplant to Andamans, not fleet combat
candidate_screen.why: Branch survival removes historical New Georgia loss
candidate_screen.transfer_cost: medium; submarine risk must be paid

recommended_initial_package_before_RN_en.basing: Singapore/Lingga with forward use through Penang/Sabang; do not park the whole group at Port Blair
recommended_initial_package_before_RN_en.mission: observation/contact handoff, escort, one-pass Type-93 night interception if a high-quality target appears
explicitly_not_included: two extra heavy cruisers before British eastbound sortie is confirmed

escalation_if_Eastern_Fleet_leaves_Ceylo.second_gate: Suzuya/Kumano pair only if British fleet persists into Bay/Andaman approach and Central Pacific risk permits
escalation_if_Eastern_Fleet_leaves_Ceylo.submarine_gate: conventional submarine reinforcement first; high-speed-submerged boats only after fresh contact geometry justifies their repositioning advantage
